newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's health workers consider other strikes.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's health workers consider other strikes.

text.p: Morocco's public health workers' union said on Friday that members were looking at the possibility of holding other strikes after ending a three-day stoppage on Thursday.
"We will meet soon to assess the situation and study ways to pursue the struggle, including strikes," a spokesman for the Democratic Labour Confederation (CDT) told Reuters.
He said authorities had not responded to their claims for pay increases and compensation for medical risks despite what he called successful industrial action.
"Up to 90 percent of workers observed the strike all over the country," he added. Their action was capped by a sit-in outside the health ministry on Thursday.
"The government has remained mute in the face of our demands...and security forces prevented us from entering the ministry, but we stayed outside from 8 a.m. to 8.p.m.," he said.
Two unions were involved in the strike, the CDT and General Union of Moroccan workers (UGTM), during which emergency services were maintained.
The unions say there are 3,500 doctors and 40,000 paramedical staff in the public sector.
